definitions.explanation: A vertical line of broken threads in stockings, pantyhose, or tights — what English speakers call a 'run' (US) or 'ladder' (UK). Also used as a する verb: {伝線|でんせん}する 'to get a run/ladder.'

examples.japanese: ストッキングが{伝線|でんせん}した。
{爪|つめ}が{引|ひ}っかかって{伝線|でんせん}してしまった。
examples.english: My nail caught on them and they ran.

examples.japanese: {出勤|しゅっきん}{途中|とちゅう}でストッキングが{伝線|でんせん}したので、コンビニで{新|あたら}しいのを{買|か}った。
examples.english: My stockings got a run on the way to work, so I bought a new pair at a convenience store.

notes:
Originally meaning 'transmission line' / 'spreading along a line', here applied to the way a tiny snag in stockings rapidly propagates along a vertical thread. Used as both noun and する verb.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {伝線|でんせん}する: to get a run
- {伝線|でんせん}{防止|ぼうし}: run-resistant
- {伝線|でんせん}しにくいストッキング: run-resistant stockings

NOTE ON HOMOPHONES:
Three common words share the reading でんせん: {伝線|でんせん} (this entry, a run in stockings), {伝染|でんせん} (contagion/transmission of disease), and {電線|でんせん} (electric wire). Context almost always disambiguates them.
